claims.statement: The backend dependency direction is strict: transport → app → domain ← infra. Domain has zero framework imports (no Gin, no GORM, no Redis, no asynq); only Go stdlib and internal/pkg/clock.

The frontend splits by role (admin, partner, adv-partner, employee, accountant) and by viewport (desktop pages + a parallel pages/mobile/* tree), with ResponsivePage.tsx and MobileBottomNav.tsx as the dual-layout primitives.
Every frontend change must cover desktop and mobile for every affected role; mobile breakpoints to verify are 390px and 320px, and touch targets must be at least 44px.
All UI text is Vietnamese; there is no i18n layer — strings are inline in components or in DTO tables.

The system has three distinct async surfaces: domain events (Redis Streams, ADR-004), asynq background jobs (Redis queues, ADR-005), and payment-provider IPN webhooks (HTTP). They share infrastructure but not semantics.

Wallet payments reach a terminal state only via the IPN-driven state machine (ipn_completed, ipn_failed, ipn_reversed); the financial critical path is transactional and does not depend on event delivery for correctness.
Cache invalidation and event publishing are deferred via domain.RegisterAfterCommit callbacks that fire only after RunInTransaction commits successfully.
Production uses OnePay (never 9Pay); the system is provider-agnostic via ADR-003; the production server is x86_64/amd64.

Adding a new feature follows a fixed order: entity and rule in domain/, port in domain/ports/, implementation in infra/, service in app/services/, handler in transport/http/handlers/, route in app/bootstrap/routes.go.
